Assessment scope: independent M3 milestone Code Review, complete dcc357b4..fdcd3379 runtime/caller/test retirement against the current approved Proposal, exact RF/CLI/Workflow Design and primary Delivery package. Surviving changed subjects are bound below; deleted baseline subjects are identified separately with actual original hashes. M2's original judgment/resolved finding remains predecessor evidence and is not retargeted to changed M3 subjects. This reviewer did not edit source, tests, upstream judgments, activity or work state.

Requirement and scope alignment — pass. M3 removes compact/lifecycle/new-change dispatch, their exclusive Node engines, old stored schemas/templates/activation metadata, Python stored-state decoding/progression and dedicated positive tests. This implements the selected six-format retirement after M2 established independent v2 recording/discovery. Historical docs/changes archives remain untouched outside this initiative's own stage records. No migration, temporary legacy reader/recovery facility, new format or v2 replacement eligibility engine is introduced. The separate current public skill/resource/governing/package alignment remains M4; this judgment does not claim installed-guidance readiness.

Public boundary and errors — pass. Removed handlers/imports no longer process old bodies or requests. The entry point detects retired commands before file observability; its alternate logging-prefix inspection uses pure grammar and an empty environment, so leading valid logging flags cannot restore diagnostic file effects. Runtime help no longer advertises removed commands. Existing result rendering receives an invocation identity without enabling logging, preserving concise/detailed/human invalid-usage output. New real subprocess cases cover all three retired commands, five output formats, logging prefixes, private request data, unchanged archive bytes and absence of created root/log/transaction directories. Earlier failing concise-format and package-path cases are retained in evidence and corrected before this assessment.

V2 safety and version separation — pass. Current primary/advanced recording, neutral transport, Origin/reference/preservation, exact revision, conflict/lock, partial publication, retry and version2 recovery code is retained. All seven complete v2 modules and installed-package mutation/concurrency/recovery proof were executed after dependency retirement. Model/document explicit-recording-v1 markers and targeted/advanced schema1 transport remain separate contracts. Package inspection now requires current v2 runtime/schema modules and actively rejects retired packaged paths; the fnmatch check applies the existing catalogue rather than leaving declared forbidden patterns unenforced.

Current discovery, selectors and artifact validation — pass. The former lifecycle wrapper invokes factual schema2 workflow-context, requires success and complete scope, and does not derive eligibility. Metadata validation delegates current complete-set validation, retaining only separately contracted cache-measurement parsing. Artifact scope uses reserved v2 paths even when change.json is absent, preserves lexical selected paths for symlink validation, checks exact Git snapshots through the current validator, and excludes archival payloads from related/warning traversal. The selector routes current/malformed/residual sets to v2 validation and archive changes to retirement rejection checks; it removes old eligibility/evidence-registry selection instead of recreating it. Deletion handling does not turn a missing current reserved manifest into an empty pass. Existing standalone documents, release evidence, generated-surface and actual selected-revision protections remain.

Deferred caller ownership — pass. WorkflowAutomationStateStore and StageOwnedChangeStateStore reject immediately before path resolution, reads, locks or writes. Legacy milestone/package completion adapters explicitly reject; no new automation field mapping is invented. Generic policy, capability and receipt methods stay separate. Immutable Git anchor/tree/rename/dirty checks remain, while old post-review YAML-tail parsing/exemptions reject as unsupported. The boundary marker adapter rejects old stored authority without reading it, preserving independent boundary document/model grammar. The review adapter rejects stored roots before decoding and retains standalone review/calibration/fidelity functionality. Old CLI measurement execution is explicitly unsupported; provenance/baseline checks remain, with no fabricated savings.

Shared helper preservation — pass. Independently compared the extracted project_yaml definitions against their previous implementation ASTs: exception, Line, scalar/token/mapping/list/block and load_yaml definitions all match exactly. The module owns generic grammar and selects no stored format. Keeping configuration/measurement YAML is therefore not a retained legacy record decoder. The actual surviving imports and shared parser users were inspected alongside full affected-module evidence.

Test maintenance and adequacy — pass. Removed groups are the explicitly retired progression/activation/scaffolding/lifecycle-field settlement/stored-reference and legacy evidence-routing contracts. Their positive behavior is not owed by v2. Shared encoding, bounds, identity, exclusion, atomicity, third-state, recovery, query/diagnostic and correction-after-completion protections remain in v2; separate policy, receipts, calibration, standalone document, Git snapshot, selector/cache and package protection remain in full mixed modules. Deleting change manifests from standalone calibration/review fixtures makes their independent subject scope explicit rather than treating archived stored roots as a current operational facility. Retained public rejection tests exercise no-effects outcomes, not merely missing files or source-string matches. The actual Node count400 versus predecessor490 is reported as an observed runner count, not proof of redundancy or a performance saving.

Proof and applicability — pass for M3 scope. Current m3-legacy-runtime-removal binds34 surviving changed paths and a complete deletion inventory, the allocated caller/check-group dispositions and rollback basis. Inspected final logs for npm400/0skip, selector155, artifact109 and installed npm7; current evidence also records v2 modules168, discovery33, metadata7/query2, boundary83/reference28, cache14, automation31/state12/code-state12/policy68, standalone review109, wrapper3 and measurement/provenance4. Required complete modules ran after relevant helper/fixture changes; later deletion of unreachable definitions/unused imports is disclosed and does not alter tested execution. V1/V10 structural/readability/record/whitespace passes remain structural proof;89 existing readability warnings and historical failed audit/drift are not concealed. This reviewer did not rerun duplicate broad suites or infer a full-branch CI pass.

Checklist conclusion: approved contract alignment, scoped coverage/removal, edges/errors, architecture, compatibility, security/privacy, generated runtime/schema currency, unrelated-scope control and evidence attribution are adequate. No material M3 finding or necessary owner decision emerged. Return this judgment to route for milestone disposition and authorized M4; this review does not change work/activity. Final whole-change independent Code Review after all implementation/corrections and distinct Verify remain mandatory. No branch/PR/release/final retirement readiness is claimed.
